answer: The Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and mean expression for protein-coding genes in CD4 immune cells is r ≈ 0.062 (r = 0.0617, p ≈ 2.8e-18), using the mean raw (batch-corrected) count across the 151 CD4 samples over 19,942 exactly-matched protein-coding genes. Despite statistical significance (large n), the correlation is essentially negligible — gene length explains <0.4% of the variance in mean CD4 expression. Sensitivity analyses: mean log2(count+1) gives r = 0.3155 (modest positive), and excluding the 1,518 all-zero protein-coding genes gives r = 0.0528 (raw mean, n = 18,424) or r = 0.2652 (log mean). Under the pre-specified primary definition, the answer is a near-zero positive correlation of ~0.062.
